Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary: Acute onset (2 days) midline lower abdominal/suprapubic pain with urinary frequency and pink-tinged urine, mild nausea, subjective sweats without documented fever; no dysuria, no flank/back pain, no vaginal discharge; regular menses. No prior similar episodes. Allergy to amoxicillin. No exam or urinalysis performed.  
- Working diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (UTI) — supported by suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and hematuria; absence of dysuria does not exclude UTI (consistent with DDx).  
- Management provided: Empiric antibiotic prescribed for 3 days (twice daily; specific agent not documented) with safety-net advice to seek care if worsening pain, fever, back pain, or new symptoms; face-to-face review may be required.  
- Considerations (from DDx consistent with transcript):  
  - Ureterolithiasis/bladder stone (medium likelihood): Hematuria with suprapubic pain and frequency; less likely without colicky pain or flank pain.  
  - Early pregnancy-related issue including ectopic (low likelihood): Lower abdominal pain in reproductive-age patient; pregnancy status not assessed—testing recommended if clinically appropriate.  
  - Appendicitis (low likelihood): Mild nausea and lower abdominal pain without localization or systemic features.  
  - PID (low likelihood): No discharge, fever, or dyspareunia reported.  
- Conflicts: None between transcript and DDx noted.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute uncomplicated cystitis — Likelihood: High. Justification: Suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine (hematuria), subjective sweats; lack of dysuria does not rule out.  
- Ureterolithiasis/bladder stone — Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Hematuria with suprapubic pain/frequency; absence of flank pain and colicky features lowers likelihood.  
- Early pregnancy-related issue (including ectopic) — Likelihood: Low. Justification: Reproductive-age with lower abdominal pain; no pregnancy assessment performed; no vaginal bleeding.
